Vs.

full_judgment:
The petitioner was appointed on 1.12.87 as Typist at the Khulna Branch of the then Eastern Mercantile Bank Ltd., the name of which was changed to Pubali Bank Ltd. Respondent No. 2 and the assets including liabilities thereof was over and vested in the Respondent No. 2 Pubali Bank Ltd. The petitioner claims that since the date of his joining he had been working with the superiors and in appreciation of his service the Chief Manager of the Bank issued a certificate on 28.9.72. The petitioner claims that thereafter the Bank started harassing him by transferring him and the Bank also asked the petitioner to report to the Martial Law Administration, Khulna, on baseless allegations. The petitioner believes that he was unnecessarily harassed as he had sent anonymous letter to the high authorities of the Bank complaining of the mischief acts of certain personnel’s of the Bank resulting in heavy loss. Relying on his report the Chief Manager of the Bank sent a telegram on 7.6.75 to the Manager of the Cement Clinker & Grinding Factory, Chittagong to stop delivery of 4,000 bags of Cement favouring the vault on the fictitious ground that the permit No. TCB/CLINKER & 74-23 dated 17.4.75 had been lost. If the petitioner had not been reported the matter, the Bank would have sustained loss. He also claims that as a result of another report by him, the Bank appointed 8 additional suppliers of Medicines for supply of Medicines to the staff of the Bank in different Branches which put an end to the illegal gain by certain personnel of the Bank by buying medicines from a single supplier. He further claims that to harass him further the bank served a charge sheet dated 24.10.75 making false allegation against him and ultimately without observing any legal formalities by Memo dated 3.8.76 gave warning by way of punishment. Subsequently, the Bank terminated the services of the petitioner on 8.12.76 with effect from 15.12.76. On an appeal, the Bank, on certain undertaking dated 16.6.77 by the petitioner, appointed him on Adhoc basis by Memo dated 20.6.77 for 80 days. The petitioner claims that as the Bank did not reinstate his to him service, he withdrew his undertaking. The Bank by its Memo No. HC/ADMN/FR 1534/30361 dated 24.9.77 again gave an adhoc appointment to the petitioner. This time only for 31 days from 1.10.77 to 31.10.77 and then on an appeal by the petitioner and on several representations made by him, the Bank issued a letter of appointment on 10.6.78 effective from 10.12.77. This was also an adhoc appointment. The petitioner again requested to re-instate him to his former post with all legal benefits and sent several reminders, but the Bank, instead of re-instating him to his, post served another charge-sheet under Memo. No. Ho: PD: PF-1538 /2964 dated 27.2.81 for refusing to comply with management's instructions to submit certain certificates as demanded earlier in the appointment letter. The petitioner claims that as the certificates had already been submitted to the Bank at the time of first appointment and the Bank was to re-instate him to his previous post, he was not required to submit certificates afresh. The Petitioner, therefore, sent a grievance petition on 23.11.81. In reply to the grievance petition the Bank by Memo dated 28.11.81 directed the petitioner to appear on 14.12.81 before Mr. Aziz Ahmed, Deputy Controller, Foreign Department who was appointed the Enquiry Officer by the Bank. The petitioner appeared before the said Enquiry Officer on 14.12.81 and produced all documents in support of his case. The Bank having taken no decision after the enquiry the petitioner filed a case on 16.1.82 before the respondent No. 1 against the respondents Nos. 2-4 being complaint case No. 12 of 1982 praying, inter alia, for direction to the Bank to reinstate the petitioner to his former post with all back wages and other legal dues etc. The Bank filed the written objection on 30-3-82 stating that after holding a proper enquiry the Bank by Memo. No. HO/D. Cell /PP-1538/137/3767 dated 2.3.82 issued by the Assistant General Manager, Disciplinary Cell, Head Office, Dhaka, forwarded a copy of the said Enquiry Report to the Petitioner and asked him erroneously it found that the petitioner was to show cause by 16.3.82 why he should not be dismissed from services as he had been found guilty by the Enquiry Officer. The petitioner replied to the show cause notice on 15.3.82 alleging that the charges were wrongly framed against him and not proved against him. During the pendency of the said Complaint Case No. 12 of 1982 which was fixed for hearing on 13.5.82 the Bank not being satisfied with the petitioner's reply to the said show cause notice dated 2.3.82, dismissed the petitioner. The petitioner thereafter sent a further grievance petition on 10-4-82 requesting the bank to reconsider his case afresh and withdraw the said letter of dismissal, but the Bank, by its Memo dated 8.4.82 rejected the prayer of the petitioner, The petitioner, thereafter, filed Complaint Case No. 115 of 1982 before the Respondent No. 1 praying that he be reinstated to his former post. The learned Labour Court, Respondent No. 1, heard both the Complaint Cases No. 12 of 1982 and 115 of 1982 analogously and after considering the evidence on record, dismissed both the complaint cases by his decision and order dated 14.2.87 Annexure 'K' which is the impugned order. 

 "Whereas you Mr. Shamsur Rahman, S/O. Late Md. Shefatullah Mollah, have disclosed to the Management in writing vide your appeal dated 16th June, 1977, that the complaints made by you from time to time in the past during your previous service in this Bank as typist to the Chief Martial Law Administrator, Ministries, Governor, Bangladesh Bank etc. against Bank Management were not actually passed on facts, and you did all these things on wrong assumptions for which you repented and prayed for unconditional apology undertaking therein solemnly that you will never repeat in future any activity detrimental to the interest of the Bank or any of its officers amounting to misconduct, insubordination and indiscipline;
